studentTask.text: Today's focus: precise claims distinguished from opposing claims. Essential question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to precise claims distinguished from opposing claims change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Explain what precise claims distinguished from opposing claims means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play. You'll need: course notebook or digital equivalent; the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation; citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Welcome and retrieval: Open with a short retrieval prompt on today's lesson. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
- Set the reading purpose: State one question about today's lesson the reading must answer. The learner writes the question in their own words before reading.
- Sustained close reading: Uninterrupted reading and annotation of the assigned text, working in the grades 9-10 text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range. No instruction interrupts this block. An accessible reading representation is used if preferred.
- Evidence harvest: The learner extracts the passages bearing on today's lesson, records why each was selected, and marks the one they are least sure about.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for today's lesson, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
- If repeated error pattern: Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of today's lesson.
- If procedure without understanding: Ask the learner to explain why the move for today's lesson works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.

independentEvidenceTask.text: Read the assigned text sustained and uninterrupted, then harvest and justify the evidence bearing on today's lesson. When finished: Quote the single passage that most changes your reading of today's lesson, and say what it changes.
